skills/toil/confluence-cloud.md

Pages, spaces, CQL search, comments, labels and attachments on Confluence Cloud (https://<your-site>.atlassian.net, REST API v2, with v1 where v2 has no endpoint). Built from Atlassian’s API documentation and never run against a live site. Verification level: unit.

For Confluence Data Center or Server, use the confluence area instead. The two are separate areas because their APIs differ: Cloud’s v2 API has different paths, pages by cursor rather than offset, and addresses spaces by a numeric id rather than their key.

Supported versions: The oldest Confluence Cloud version toil supports hasn’t been established. Confluence Cloud is always current. toil calls REST API v2 (/wiki/api/v2) and, where v2 has no endpoint, v1 (/wiki/rest/api: CQL search, adding and removing labels, attachment uploads), with an Atlassian account email and API token sent as Basic auth. Nothing has been run against a live site yet.

Credential

An Atlassian account API token plus that account’s email address. Create the token at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens (Atlassian account → Security → API tokens → Create API token). toil sends Authorization: Basic base64(<email>:<apiToken>), as Atlassian documents for scripts. There is no password, OAuth app or browser login. The token acts with the account’s own permissions, so a read sees what that account can see.

The same account token works for Jira Cloud. With no token of its own, the default connection uses TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN (the default jira-cloud connection’s env value). Any other connection borrows a jira-cloud connection’s token, env or stored, only by naming it: "apiTokenFrom": "imagile-cloud". Its own token always wins, and meta.context.shared says when the token came from Jira Cloud. Only the token is borrowed: email is always this connection’s own, and must be the address the token belongs to.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_BASE_URLyesConfluence Cloud site root, without /wiki: https://<your-site>.atlassian.net
emailTOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_EMAILyesEmail address of the Atlassian account the token belongs to
apiTokenTOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_API_TOKENyesAtlassian account API token (a secret), unless borrowed from Jira Cloud
apiTokenFromTOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_API_TOKEN_FROMnoA jira-cloud connection whose token this connection uses
writesTOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

toil adds /wiki/api/v2 and /wiki/rest/api itself, so baseUrl is the site root. A baseUrl ending in /wiki (as the browser shows it) is refused with CONFIG_INVALID before anything is sent: drop the /wiki. There is no CI fallback variable. The examples use the placeholder https://confluence-cloud.imagile.dev, which never resolves; your own site is https://<your-site>.atlassian.net.

export TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_BASE_URL=https://confluence-cloud.imagile.dev
export TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_EMAIL=you@example.com
export TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_API_TOKEN=<your API token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "imagile-wiki": { "area": "confluence-cloud", "baseUrl": "https://confluence-cloud.imagile.dev", "email": "you@example.com", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "confluence-cloud": { "connection": "imagile-wiki" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add imagile-wiki --area confluence-cloud (or toil connections login imagile-wiki) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_API_TOKEN. Env vars always win over the file.

Commands

Every command also takes --connection <name>. Write commands (marked ✎) need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. Names and flags match confluence wherever the operation is the same. MCP tools are confluence_cloud_<command> (confluence_cloud_get_page). The two deletes are CLI only: they are never MCP tools.

CommandFlagsReturns
get-page--idThe page with its storage body, plus bodyText
get-page-by-title--space <key> --titleThe page with that exact title, plus bodyText
list-pages--space <key> --limit --cursorPages in the space (no bodies)
get-page-children--idDirect children, each with its type
get-page-history--idEvery version of the page
search--cql --limit --cursor --expandOne page of CQL results, as Confluence returns it
create-page ✎--space <key> --title --body --body-file --parent-id --representationThe created page, plus bodyText
update-page ✎--id --title --body --body-file --status --representationThe updated page, plus bodyText
delete-page ✎ (CLI only)--id{ deleted }
list-comments--idTop-level footer comments, each with bodyText
add-comment ✎--id --body --representationThe comment, plus bodyText
get-labels--idThe page’s labels
add-label ✎--id --labels <a,b>The labels Confluence reports
remove-label ✎--id --label{ removed, from }
list-spaces--type --limit --cursorSpaces the account can see
get-space--keyThe space, with its plain-text description
list-attachments--id <page-id>The page’s attachments
upload-attachment ✎--id <page-id> --file --commentThe attachments Confluence created
download-attachment--id <attachment-id> --dir{ saved, filename, size }
delete-attachment ✎ (CLI only)--id <attachment-id>{ deleted }
toil confluence-cloud get-page-by-title --space DOCS --title "Release notes"
toil confluence-cloud search --cql 'space=DOCS AND type=page AND text~"runbook"' --limit 10
toil confluence-cloud create-page --space DOCS --title Runbook --body-file runbook.html --parent-id 12345 --allow-write
toil confluence-cloud update-page --id 12345 --title "Release notes (archived)" --allow-write
toil confluence-cloud download-attachment --id att98765 --dir downloads

Ids and keys

Page ids are numbers (12345); attachment ids carry an att prefix (att98765). Commands that take --space take the space key (DOCS), as confluence does; toil looks up the numeric space id v2 needs with one extra request, and a key that matches nothing is NOT_FOUND. An id containing /, \, ? or # is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent, and the rest is percent-encoded as one path segment.

Body format: storage

Bodies are storage format, the XHTML Confluence keeps pages in, both ways:

  • Out: every page and comment is read with body-format=storage, so body.storage.value is the XHTML. Beside it, bodyText is a plain-text rendering: tags dropped, blocks on their own lines, list items as - , table cells joined with |, code macro text kept, macro parameters dropped. It’s for reading, not for writing back.
  • In (--body, --body-file): storage-format XHTML, or wiki markup with --representation wiki, which Confluence converts to storage. Atlassian Document Format isn’t offered.

confluence’s --markdown isn’t here: Confluence Cloud documents no synchronous Markdown converter. Write storage XHTML, or wiki markup, instead. get-page has no --expand: v2 has no expansions, and the body always comes back.

Paging

Lists page by cursor. Without --limit, list-pages and list-spaces read every page of results. With --limit N they return at most N, and meta.page.nextCursor resumes: pass it back as --cursor with --limit. Every other list (get-page-children, get-page-history, list-comments, get-labels, list-attachments) is read in full. Paging stops after 1,000 requests with an error naming the list.

search returns one page, as Confluence returns it (results, size, totalSize, _links), 25 results unless --limit says otherwise. When there are more, meta.page.nextCursor is the cursor from its _links.next: pass it as --cursor (with the same --cql) for the next page. confluence’s --start isn’t here: Cloud search pages by cursor.

Notes

  • update-page reads the page first and sends the next version number, keeping the title unless --title is given. Confluence Cloud requires a body on every update, so with no --body or --body-file the current storage body is sent back unchanged (a rename). --status draft sends version 1, as Atlassian documents for a change to draft, and deletes any draft the page already has. --representation without a body is INVALID_INPUT.
  • create-page without --parent-id puts the page under the space’s homepage, as the API does.
  • get-page-children uses v2’s direct children, which lists folders, whiteboards, databases and embeds beside child pages; each result’s type says which.
  • get-page-history returns the version list (number, createdAt, authorId, message, minorEdit), where confluence returns Data Center’s history object.
  • list-comments reads footer comments only, top level only: no replies and no inline comments. add-comment adds a footer comment.
  • add-label and remove-label use v1, since v2 can’t write labels. Labels are added with the global prefix. remove-label sends the label as a query parameter, so any label can be removed.
  • upload-attachment uses v1 multipart with X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck, and always adds a new attachment. The file name is the path’s last segment, with / or \ splitting it on every platform.
  • download-attachment reads the attachment, then fetches its downloadLink under baseUrl/wiki with the credential. Confluence answers with a redirect to a signed URL on Atlassian’s media host; toil follows it with every header dropped, so the credential stays on your site. It saves under .toil/ (or --dir), keeping only the file name, and never replaces a file that’s already there.
  • delete-page and delete-attachment move the item to the trash; neither purges.
  • A 429 is retried after the delay Confluence asks for, as in every area.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Confluence Cloud site root, without /wiki: https://<your-site>.atlassian.net

    TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_BASE_URL

  • email required

    Email address of the Atlassian account the API token belongs to

    TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_EMAIL

  • apiToken required secret

    Atlassian account API token

    TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_API_TOKEN

  • apiTokenFrom

    The jira-cloud connection to take apiToken from when this connection has none

    TOIL_CONFLUENCE_CLOUD_API_TOKEN_FROM

Commands at a glance

  • toil confluence-cloudget-page

    Get a Confluence Cloud page by ID, with its storage-format body

    MCP confluence_cloud_get_page--id <page-id>

  • toil confluence-cloudget-page-by-title

    Find a Confluence Cloud page by space key and exact title

    MCP confluence_cloud_get_page_by_title--space <key>--title <title>

  • toil confluence-cloudlist-pages

    List pages in a Confluence Cloud space (consider --output-file for large results)

    MCP confluence_cloud_list_pages--space <key>--limit <n>--cursor <cursor>

  • toil confluence-cloudget-page-children

    Get the direct children of a Confluence Cloud page

    MCP confluence_cloud_get_page_children--id <page-id>

  • toil confluence-cloudget-page-history

    Get the versions of a Confluence Cloud page

    MCP confluence_cloud_get_page_history--id <page-id>

  • toil confluence-cloudsearch

    Search Confluence Cloud with CQL

    MCP confluence_cloud_search--cql <query>--limit <n>--cursor <cursor>--expand <fields>

  • toil confluence-cloudcreate-pagewrite

    Create a new Confluence Cloud page

    MCP confluence_cloud_create_page--space <key>--title <title>--body <html>--body-file <path>--parent-id <id>--representation <format>--allow-write

  • toil confluence-cloudupdate-pagewrite

    Update a Confluence Cloud page (fetches the current version automatically)

    MCP confluence_cloud_update_page--id <page-id>--title <title>--body <html>--body-file <path>--status <status>--representation <format>--allow-write

  • toil confluence-clouddelete-pagewriteCLI only

    Delete a Confluence Cloud page (moves it to the trash; does not purge it)

    --id <page-id>--allow-write

  • toil confluence-cloudlist-comments

    List footer comments on a Confluence Cloud page

  • toil confluence-cloudadd-commentwrite

    Add a footer comment to a Confluence Cloud page

  • toil confluence-cloudget-labels

    Get labels on a Confluence Cloud page

  • toil confluence-cloudadd-labelwrite

    Add labels to a Confluence Cloud page

    MCP confluence_cloud_add_label--id <page-id>--labels <names>--allow-write

  • toil confluence-cloudremove-labelwrite
